newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt delay no surprise - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt delay no surprise - analysts.

text.p: Russia's announcement on Monday that it will delay settling old Soviet debts with commercial creditors early next year is no surprise, though prices on the secondary market may slip in reaction, analysts said.
A finance ministry official said the restructuring deal was unlikely to be closed until the first quarter of 1997.
"It was already in the price," Chase analyst Robin Hubbard said.
The emerging debt market has already closed for the U.S. Veteran's Day holiday.

However, prices for the debt had firmed in the morning in light volume on increasing optimism over the outlook for Russia, especially with a Eurobond in the offing and reports that President Boris Yeltsin is recovering well from his heart operation.
Bank of America analyst, Richard Gray, said even though the delay was anticipated, there could be some disappointed selling when the market reopens on Tuesday.
Moscow and its creditors have all but wrapped up a deal on the about $32 billion of commercial debt which Russia took on after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
The agreement is now going through a lengthy reconciliation process to match up the thousands of creditors.
Many traders and analysts expect debt prices to rise further especially if the imminent Russian Eurobond, as is widely predicted, is priced at a relatively tight spread.
But the debt has already risen some 150 percent this year and further substantial rises are unlikely, some analysts said.
"We are still positive overall, but at these levels there isn't a lot more to go for," Hubbard said.
